notes: Clear icon tile + large title + 3 benefit rows; single primary CTA pinned with page dots.
Benefit row 3 repeats the subtitle's 'no internet, no cloud' - mild copy redundancy.
Large empty band between benefits and footer is acceptable for a welcome page.
Empty state is obvious: glyph, title, one-line reason, full-width Connect CTA.
Status pills under the large title read well; SIMULATED badge intentional.
Empty-state block sits slightly below optical centre and the CTA floats mid-screen rather than in the bottom action zone used by the connected state (layout jumps after connect).
State legible in <1 s: green tinted hero, flat arm, 'Lowered' title + plain-language subtitle.
Disabled Lower uses the neutral disabled style with an 'Already lowered.' hint - good.
Subtitle 'Signed in 0.54 s · phone-measured' is engineering wording on the primary screen; 'phone-measured' adds nothing for a driver.
~160 pt dead band between the chips row and the action dock.
Idle STOP is a pale tinted button; fine, but low emphasis relative to its safety role is a judgement call.
Best state of the set: blue hero, moving arm, 'Raising', progress '0.8 s of about 4.0 s' + bar, STOP becomes solid red primary while Lower/Raise disable with 'Arm is moving. Use Stop.'
Upright arm + 'Raised' + 'Your space is reserved' - unambiguous.
Primary action switches to green Lower; disabled Raise with hint. Good.
Amber hero with mid-angle arm and clear instruction 'Raise or lower to continue'.
No hint line above the buttons in this state, so the dock separator jumps ~26 pt up compared with every other state - visible layout shift between states.
Guard banner is good: title, bullet reason, plain-language fix, 'Safety checks >' link, dismiss X.

Raise is rendered in a THIRD button style (light tinted fill + blue label) that is neither the enabled filled style nor the neutral disabled style; a user cannot tell whether Raise is tappable or blocked. Contradicts the 'one neutral disabled style' rule.

Mixed message: hero stays green 'Lowered - You can drive in' while an amber line under it says 'Movement blocked'; four competing accent colours (green hero, amber chip+banner, blue Raise, red STOP) on one screen.
Zone-blocked chip correctly uses icon + text (not colour only).

Red hero with dashed 'unknown' arm, warning glyph + 'Fault', 'Sensors: see fault' chip, and an explicit recovery card ('Hold the unit button for 8 seconds. The app cannot clear a fault.'). Controls locked with hint; STOP still available.
Hero subtitle 'Position sensors disagree' and card text 'The wrong end-limit switch fired, or both fired at once' describe the same thing in two vocabularies.
Recovery card's heading/body/hint use three text weights in a tight stack; slightly dense.
Neutral hero, dashed ghost arm and '?' glyph; title 'Position unknown' and instruction 'Lower it to home the barrier' match the enabled green Lower + disabled Raise with hint.
The small '?' glyph floating at the top of the hero looks like a tappable help button but is decorative; consider removing or making it a real info affordance.

Connection-lost card with reason and full-width Reconnect at top; hero switches to 'Last known: Raising / Not live' with desaturated arm; chips switch to clock icons; all controls (incl. STOP) disabled with 'Controls are off while offline.' - excellent stale-state handling.
Chips row is cut horizontally in half by the action dock at the fold; reads as a clip rather than an intentional scroll edge. Add bottom content inset or a fade under the dock.
Disabled STOP glyph/label grey is low-emphasis by design but the disabled STOP is the same neutral style as Lower/Raise - fine.
Modal with Close, large title, NEARBY BARRIERS section, one inset row with BT avatar, 'Previously paired' badge, signal bars and chevron; 'Scan again' text action.
Signal-strength bars have no text/value (icon only) - fine visually, but provide an accessibility label.
No visible 'scanning' indicator next to the section header; if the list is live, a small spinner would clarify state.
Grouped inset lists with section headers, right-aligned values, check glyphs for interlocks; power card starts above the fold so scrolling is obvious.

Header has an icon-only circular cloud-off control next to the Connected pill: unlabeled, looks like a button, meaning (local only) is not obvious. Use the same 'Local only' text pill as the Barrier tab or drop it.
'Barrier's last counter' is protocol detail on a user-facing tab; state values (Raised / Done / No fault) are all plain grey - the barrier state is not emphasised.
'Zone clear - Clear' and 'Sensors valid - Valid' repeat the label in the value.
Empty state itself is good (glyph, title, reason, Connect CTA).

More than half of the screen is a REQUIREMENTS list of course/spec codes (C4, C5, S5, S6, 'Bench', 'Board', 'Nothing here is a verdict...'). This is grader/engineering content on a primary user tab and dominates the empty state; a driver cannot act on any of it.
Wording inconsistency: pill says 'Not connected' here vs 'Disconnected' on the Barrier tab.
Same unlabeled cloud-off icon button in the header as health-connected.
Large title + 'Share CSV' action, 4-segment filter, collapsible Evidence summary, inset list with typed icons and monospace-ish timestamps, destructive 'Clear log' at the end.
'Share CSV' is a large tinted pill in the title row; on Android/iOS this is normally a toolbar icon or text button - feels heavy next to the large title.
Paired rows ('Lower: Moving' / 'State Lowering') are visually equal weight; commands vs state changes could be differentiated more (e.g. state rows in secondary style).
Row metadata strings ('#3 · 73 ms · simulated') are dense but acceptable for an evidence log.
Grouped inset sections with footers; disabled Bluetooth segment shows lock + explanatory footer - clear.
Segmented controls are wrapped inside a white card, producing a card-in-card double frame; native settings place segments directly in the row or use a picker row.
Haptics row has no leading icon while every other navigable row has a filled blue icon tile - inconsistent row anatomy.
Toggle thumb overhangs the track (web switch rendering) - acceptable on Android but not first-party iOS-like.
Back to Settings, SIMULATED badge, large title, grouped scenario rows with step count + FSM-row chips and chevrons; sticky 'Exit presenter' bar.
List separators here are full-bleed while every other inset list insets them to the text - minor inconsistency.
Last row is cut under the sticky Exit bar without a fade; acceptable since the list obviously scrolls.
Two option cards; selected card has accent border, tint and check; unavailable option is greyed with a lock note explaining why.
Icon treatment differs between the two cards: disabled card has a filled grey icon tile, selected card has a bare outline icon with no tile - looks like two different components.
Disabled card title/body grey on white is legible but close to the lower contrast bound for title-weight text.
Classic permission-priming screen: icon tile, title, purpose copy, primary Allow + 'Not now'.
In simulator mode (previous step) asking for Bluetooth is slightly odd; consider skipping or stating it is for later real-hardware use.
Large empty mid-section; acceptable.
Three numbered step cards with trailing icons and a 1:00 'not started' ring; primary 'Start 60 s timer' + 'Skip for now'.
Step 1 says 'Tap Start' but the button is labelled 'Start 60 s timer'; step 3 refers to a 'Connect' button that does not exist on this screen - copy/controls mismatch.
Trailing icons (hand, stopwatch, keypad) are decorative and the keypad icon for 'Tap Connect' is semantically off.
Timer ring in the middle card competes with the step text; could be the screen's hero instead.
Success tile, 'You're all set.', next-step instruction and 'Go to controls' CTA.
Instruction asks the user to tap 'Connect to barrier' later; the CTA could do this directly or the button name could be emphasised.
Very large empty area; acceptable.
Textbook grouped detail list with footer explanation and a separated destructive row with consequence footer.
Counters are technical but explained in the footer.
Back, large title, app icon, name, team line, version rows, privacy and scope sections.
Large title 'About' immediately followed by a second bold 'M010 Barrier' title - double heading.
'Firmware interface: November 2026 contract' and the footer reference to 'final design review (slide 15)' are project-internal; end users will not understand them.
Long value 'November 2026 contract' nearly collides with its label on a 390 pt screen; will wrap/clip with larger text sizes.
Sheet with title + Done, explanatory intro, one inset list of 7 checks; the failing one uses amber '!' + reason + fix + 'Blocked your last command' - easy to scan, not colour-only.
Sheet title is ~24 pt bold, not the large-title style used elsewhere (acceptable for a sheet).
Many subtitles just restate the title ('Sensors valid / Valid', 'No fault latched / No fault', 'Owner phone connected / Owner').
Failing row stacks three text styles (grey subtitle, black body, amber caption) - dense.
Stepper (Connected / Securing / Checking owner / Ready) with done/active/pending glyphs, plus an 'Enter the passkey' help card with a mock Android dialog.
Subtitle 'Securing (pairing)...' duplicates the active step label directly below it.
Mock dialog text ('Bluetooth pairing request') is low-contrast grey on grey; acceptable as illustration but borderline legibility.
Step pager (1-6), step card with Ready badge, command, expectation, FSM chip and 'Up next', then the live hero, then Live status; sticky transport bar.
Transport bar has three icon-only buttons (reset, tune, previous) next to two labelled ones - unlabeled icons on a projector demo; previous is disabled with a very faint glyph.
Step pager circles are 44 pt but numbers are small for a projector.
Result card is clear: 'As expected' badge, checked expectations (result/state/guard mask), frame timing and the driver-facing message.

The step card is so tall that the arm hero is pushed below the fold - on a projector the audience cannot see the barrier and the result at the same time. Consider collapsing the details or placing a compact arm thumbnail in the card.
Codes (REJECTED_GUARD, 0x10) are acceptable per presenter brief.
Same strong result-card pattern; 'Up next: STOP still works in FAULT' helps narration.
Hero (fault arm) again starts below the fold; only a dashed sliver is visible above the transport bar, which looks like a rendering artifact.
'Not allowed from this position / Fault is latched' uses a slash join - better as two lines.
Clear expectation list and monospace frame hex.
Hero pushed below fold; arm tip peeking above the transport bar reads as a clip.
'Before the FSM table' chip is cryptic even for a presenter.
Latency stats row, histogram with spec line, +/-100 ms steppers and Tight/Typical/Wide segment; Live status and chips below.
Live status rows use a left label / left-aligned bold value two-column layout, unlike the right-aligned value rows on Health and This barrier - inconsistent list pattern.
Histogram note 'Bar height is relative to the busiest bin' with a single bar is noise; '2.0 s spec' label is right-aligned to the dashed line rather than centred on it.
Secondary 'None' under 'No command yet' / 'No fault' repeats the primary value.
Footer 'Barrier Controller (simulated): LOWERED / NONE / no fault' is raw debug text.
